angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 130,026 km at 1.83 pc = 0.95 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 546.9759 +/- 0.0401 mas (same row, RUWE 1.08): 1.83 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.1869 +/- 0.0012 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 699: radius in solar radii, 0.1869 +/- 0.0012, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112): 130,026 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.146 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 699: mass 0.146 solar masses from the K-band mass-luminosity relation of Henry & McCarthy (1993), not a dynamical mass (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3222 +/- 10 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 699: effective temperature in K, 3222 +/- 10, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 699: effective temperature in K, 3222 +/- 10, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/barnards-star.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.059, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Barnard's star (pscomppars): spectral type M3.5-4 V, from González Hernández et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A..79G/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Barnard's star (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.56 dex, from González Hernández et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A..79G/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Barnard's star (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -2.44977, from González Hernández et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A..79G/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Barnard's star (pscomppars): rotation period 142 d, from González Hernández et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A..79G/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, NAME Barnard's star: projected rotation speed 3.08 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2024A&A...687A.205M)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
